title: Build a protein language model from scratch
summary: Train a small ESM-style protein LM via masked-residue prediction. Use it for variant effect prediction + functional embedding extraction. Compare against ESM-2. The capstone for understanding bio-ML by building it.
contentIntro:
## What you'll build

Four milestones: a working ESM-style protein language model + an embedding-extraction baseline + a variant effect predictor + an analysis vs ESM-2.

- Masked-residue pretraining on UniRef
- Embedding extraction + downstream classifier
- Variant effect prediction
- Comparison with ESM-2

By the end you understand exactly how protein LMs work because you've trained one.

## What you'll build

Four milestones, ~6 weeks. PyTorch + a single GPU (16-24GB recommended). Train a small protein LM (~30M parameters) on a subset of UniRef. The model is small; the experiment is the point.

contentGrad:
## What you'll build

A reference protein LM implementation + understanding of when bio-LMs help vs when they don't. Defense covers: why structural information emerges from sequence-only pretraining, the practical use cases (embeddings, variant effects, design), and where pLMs are headed (multimodal foundation models like ESM-3).

milestones.title: Masked-residue pretraining
milestones.description:
Implement an ESM-style protein LM:

1. **Tokenizer**: 20 amino acids + 5 special tokens (PAD, MASK, BOS, EOS, UNK). Vocab=25.
2. **Architecture**: standard transformer encoder. ~12 layers; d_model = 384; heads = 6. ~30M params.
3. **Training data**: download UniRef50 (or a subset, ~1M sequences if compute is tight).
4. **Objective**: BERT-style masked-residue prediction. Mask 15% of residues; predict masked tokens.
5. **Training**: AdamW, lr 1e-4, batch size 64, sequence length 512. Train for ~1-2 epochs.

Measure:
- Per-step loss curve.
- Held-out perplexity on UniRef sequences not in training.
- Time to convergence (loss plateau).

In your writeup: training curves; the masked-residue accuracy at convergence (typically 30-40%); commentary on why structural information might emerge from this objective.

criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether the implementation is correct: tokenizer, transformer encoder, masked-residue objective with proper masking strategy (15% mask, 80% mask token / 10% random / 10% unchanged).
Score whether training is stable and converges to non-trivial masked-residue accuracy.
Score the writeup's discussion of why sequence-only pretraining might capture structural information.

milestones.title: Embedding extraction + downstream classifier
milestones.description:
Use your trained pLM as a frozen feature extractor for a downstream task.

Pick a task with available labeled data:
- **Subcellular localization** (DeepLoc dataset): predict protein's cellular compartment.
- **Enzyme function (EC number)** classification: predict enzymatic activity from sequence.
- **Stability prediction**: predict thermal stability from sequence.

Pipeline:
1. Pass labeled proteins through your frozen pLM.
2. Extract per-residue features (or pool to per-protein).
3. Train a small MLP classifier on top.
4. Evaluate on held-out test set.

Compare with:
- **Random baseline**: classifier on random features. Sanity check.
- **ESM-2 (small)** features: same pipeline with ESM-2-650M frozen.
- **One-hot + classifier**: just amino-acid identity, no learned features.

Report accuracy/F1 across all four. Expected: your pLM > one-hot > random. ESM-2 > your pLM (ESM-2 trained on much more data).

In your writeup: comparison table + discussion of where your model matches ESM-2 vs lags.

criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether the downstream pipeline is correct: frozen pLM feature extraction, MLP classifier, proper train/test split.
Score whether the comparison table covers all four conditions and the analysis is fair.
Score the writeup's analysis of why ESM-2 outperforms (data scale + architecture).

milestones.title: Variant effect prediction
milestones.description:
Adapt your pLM to predict the effect of mutations.

**Method**: log-likelihood ratio between wild-type and mutant.

```
for each variant (wild-type → mutant):
    score_wt = pLM(wild_type)  # log-likelihood at the mutated position
    score_mut = pLM(mutant)
    effect_score = score_wt - score_mut  # higher → more disruptive
```

Dataset: ProteinGym (substitutions; ~1.5M variants across ~80 proteins) or a subset.

Measure:
- **Spearman correlation** between predicted effect score and experimental fitness.
- **AUROC** on classifying functional vs neutral variants.

Compare against:
- **BLOSUM62 score**: simplest baseline (pure substitution-matrix score for the substitution).
- **ESM-2** with the same scoring procedure.

In your writeup: per-protein and aggregate Spearman correlations. Where does your pLM beat the BLOSUM baseline? Where does ESM-2 beat your pLM?

criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether the LL-ratio scoring is implemented correctly and applied to a real variant dataset.
Score whether the comparison includes BLOSUM62 and ESM-2 with proper Spearman + AUROC metrics.
Score whether the writeup breaks down performance per protein (where does the pLM excel? Where does it fail?).

milestones.title: Final analysis + recommendation
milestones.description:
Synthesis. Final report covering:

1. **Comparison table**: rows = (random, your pLM, ESM-2-650M, one-hot baseline). Columns = pretraining loss, downstream task accuracy, variant prediction Spearman, training compute.

2. **Where your pLM matches ESM-2**: which tasks does scale not matter for? Why?

3. **Where your pLM lags**: which tasks does scale + data matter for? What would close the gap?

4. **Engineering recommendation**: for a hypothetical lab choosing between (a) using off-the-shelf ESM-2, (b) training their own small pLM, (c) fine-tuning ESM-2 on their data — which would you pick for what use case?

5. **What's next**: structural pretraining (ProstT5, ESM-3), generative pLMs (ProtGPT2), domain-specific pLMs. For each, briefly: what would it buy you?

This milestone is the synthesis. The grader looks for engineering judgment + clear understanding of when scale + data + architecture matter for bio-ML.

criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether the comparison covers all four conditions on the four metrics consistently.
Score whether the recommendation engages with real trade-offs (when is training your own worth it vs using ESM-2).
Score the depth of the discussion of structural pretraining, generative pLMs, etc.
